Global Product & Engineering Relationship
·        Represent EMEA’s consent and privacy product requirements with the relevant global product and engineering teams. Ensure regional requirements are understood and reflected in planning and roadmap decisions, track global developments that affect the EMEA roadmap, and build the relationships required to drive alignment and delivery without formal authority.
Cross-Functional Collaboration
·        This role operates at the intersection of multiple functions and global teams - strong influencing skills and the ability to drive alignment without formal authority are essential.
What this role is not
This role does not own privacy policy, regulatory interpretation or compliance - that sits with Privacy. It does not own GTM strategy, positioning or sales activation - that sits with the relevant GTM teams. It is not a project management role. This role owns the product requirements, roadmap, prioritisation and technical readiness for the domain
What we need for this role
To be successful, you will possess the following skills and attributes:
·        10+ years of experience in product management, ideally within AdTech, CTV, data, and/or privacy technology.
·        Strong understanding of CTV and streaming ad products - how they are built, how they deliver, and how they are sold, and the related privacy and regulatory requirements.
·        Ability to hold commercial and technical perspectives simultaneously and find the connection between them.
·        Proven track record of owning product requirements and delivering products through engineering or product teams.
·        Experience managing a product roadmap, prioritising requirements and coordinating dependencies across multiple teams.
·        Ability to translate complex business, legal or policy requirements into clear product specifications.
·        Technically literate - able to engage directly with product and engineering teams on requirements and technical dependencies.
·        Experience working with global product or engineering teams and influencing roadmap prioritisation.
·        Strong stakeholder management skills and the ability to work across different functions and seniority levels.
·        Exceptional written and verbal communication skills.
·        Action-oriented self-starter comfortable with ambiguity and able to lead a product domain independently.
Additional experience and expertise that would be helpful:
·        Consent management or privacy technology.
·        IAB Europe Transparency & Consent Framework (TCF).
·        Pan-European experience in media or ad tech preferred.
Deep privacy or legal expertise is not required. The role will work closely with dedicated Privacy specialists who own regulatory interpretation and compliance.
What does success look like?
Success will be evident when consent and privacy-related products have clear ownership, a well-defined roadmap, and are evolving alongside the needs of our advertising, data and measurement products.
Privacy and Product operate as close partners, with regulatory requirements translated into clear product requirements and incorporated early in the development process. Our global product and engineering teams understand ESBO's priorities and treat the region as a valued input into roadmap decisions.
Ultimately, the role is successful when consent is a well-managed product domain — with the right requirements anticipated, prioritised and delivered rather than becoming blockers later in the product lifecycle.

• Make sound decisions and exercise judgement, including under time pressure.

Trintech is an award-winning, AI-driven FinTech SaaS organisation and we’re seeking an ambitious Sales Director to lead our UKI Commercial Sales team. This is a high-impact leadership role in one of Trintech's fastest-growing markets.
You will inherit a team with momentum, a proven product and significant headroom. The UKI Commercial team grew exponentially last year, with much of that growth coming from new business. Average deal size has increased significantly over the past three years, and the team is now working against a materially higher target with the UK remaining one of our largest addressable markets in EMEA.
Your job is to build on that progress and develop a high-performance culture, develop sellers, create a more proactive pipeline engine and personally influence the deals that matter. You will have the remit to shape how we grow the market - across Sales, Marketing, Partners and Solutions Consulting - rather than simply manage an existing number.
What you’ll do
• Lead the next phase of UKI growth: Turn strong momentum into repeatable, sustainable growth across new business and the wider commercial market.
• Build a proactive growth engine: Increase self-generated pipeline and reduce reliance on inbound demand by creating a clear outbound rhythm, using market insight, campaigns, partners and seller activity.
• Coach from the front: Develop sellers across prospecting, qualification, multi-threading, executive engagement, competitive positioning, negotiation and closing. This is a hands-on leadership role, not a role managed from the spreadsheet.
• Stay close to customers and deals: Join strategic customer conversations, challenge deal strategy, help unlock executive access and coach the team through complex sales cycles.
• Run the business through data: Use pipeline creation, conversion, win rates, deal size, forecast accuracy and productivity to identify where performance can improve - and act quickly.
• Create operating discipline: Own forecasting, pipeline reviews and QBRs; set clear expectations; and address gaps early and constructively.
• Shape the market strategy: Influence territory design, long-range planning and where we invest. Work across Marketing, Partners, Customer Success, Solutions Consulting and Sales Operations to build the funnel and remove growth constraints.
What you’ll bring
• A proven SaaS sales leader with evidence of delivering growth and a clear point of view on how that growth was created.
• A coach who raises the standard of the whole team, not simply the performance of the top sellers.
• A commercially curious operator who can diagnose a funnel, identify gaps and mobilise Sales, Marketing and Partners around the right actions.
• A leader who is comfortable with both strategy and detail: long-range planning one moment, deal coaching and customer meetings the next.
• Strong command of pipeline management, forecasting, conversion metrics and sales productivity.
• A customer-facing leader who enjoys executive conversations and is willing to get personally involved when it can change the outcome.
• Experience in a competitive B2B SaaS environment. Exposure to finance technology, ERP ecosystems or complex solution selling is valuable, but not essential.
• High standards and the ability to create a culture of accountability, learning and winning together.
At our core, Trintechers stand committed to fostering a culture rooted in our core values – Humble, Empowered, Reliable, and Open. Together, these values guide our actions, define our identity, and inspire us to continuously strive for excellence in everything we do.

Job Description:
WHY THIS ROLE MATTERS
Accurate and timely incentive compensation administration is essential to ensuring employees understand and trust how their performance translates into compensation. As SkinHealth Systems continues to grow internationally, the Senior Incentive Compensation Analyst, OUS provides analytical and operational support for international incentive compensation programs.
This role supports recurring compensation calculations, data validation, participant tracking, reporting, reconciliation and payment processes in accordance with approved incentive plans and established controls, including applicable SOX requirements. Working closely with Total Rewards and cross-functional partners, the Senior Analyst helps maintain accurate compensation data, identify and resolve discrepancies, and ensure incentive compensation activities are completed accurately and on schedule across international markets.
WHAT YOU’LL DO
• Support recurring administration of incentive compensation plans for international employees, including participant tracking, data preparation, calculation support, validation, reconciliation, and payment coordination.
• Prepare and validate incentive compensation calculations using approved plan provisions, established methodologies, and applicable sales and performance data.
• Collect, consolidate, and review compensation inputs from Sales Operations, Finance, Payroll, HR, and regional stakeholders to ensure completeness and accuracy prior to calculation and payment.
• Maintain incentive compensation trackers, calculation files, participant records, plan documentation, and supporting materials in accordance with established processes and SOX requirements.
• Research calculation and data discrepancies and coordinate with appropriate stakeholders to resolve routine issues, escalating complex matters or plan interpretation questions as appropriate.
• Process employee changes impacting incentive compensation, including new hires, transfers, promotions, leaves, terminations, territory changes, and other organizational changes.
• Assist with implementation of approved new or revised incentive compensation plans by updating calculation tools, templates, participant information, and supporting documentation.
• Perform testing and validation of compensation calculations and process changes using established requirements and expected outcomes.
• Prepare recurring incentive compensation reports and analyses, including payout, attainment, adjustment, and reconciliation reporting.
• Support reconciliation of incentive compensation calculations and payments with Payroll and Finance records and assist with resolution of identified discrepancies.
• Respond to routine incentive compensation inquiries and provide calculation details or supporting information, escalating complex questions and exceptions as appropriate.
• Collaborate with other members of the incentive compensation function to support process alignment, data validation, issue resolution and continuity of operations across incentive compensation programs organization-wide.
• Support periodic audits and reviews by gathering requested documentation, calculation support, and other relevant records.
• Identify administrative or process improvement opportunities and provide recommendations to Total Rewards leadership.
• Perform other duties as assigned.
WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR
Required
• Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Business Administration, Human Resources, or a related field.

Technical & Quality Centre
Quality Product Analysis Specialist
Location: Rotherham
Alliance Automotive Group UK & Ireland is a leading distributor of passenger and commercial vehicle parts to motor factors, garages, franchise networks and public services throughout the UK and Ireland. Our strategically designed network, supported by acquisitions, positions us as a market leader in providing automotive parts distribution services to the aftermarket.
Supported by a top-tier logistics network comprising over 300 local stores, 20 Regional Distribution Centres, our state-of-the-art 1 million square foot National Distribution Centre, and a workforce of over 6,000 colleagues, our business model prioritises maintaining an extensive and readily available product range to uphold the quality of our service offerings.
The Quality Product Analysis Specialist plays a critical role within the Technical & Quality Centre by conducting in-depth inspections, diagnostic testing, and root cause analysis of returned automotive components.
This position ensures that warranty claims are assessed accurately and consistently while supporting overall product quality, compliance, and continuous improvement initiatives.
Working across a broad range of systems—including turbochargers, braking components, suspension units, clutches, and rotating electrics (alternators and starters)—the specialist applies advanced mechanical and electrical expertise to determine failure causes, verify product performance against factory specifications, and differentiate between manufacturing defects and usage-related issues.
The role combines hands-on technical evaluation with detailed digital reporting and cross-functional collaboration. Using specialized testing equipment and precision measuring tools, the specialist generates comprehensive inspection reports, documents findings with photographic evidence, and supports warranty decision-making in alignment with company policies and regulatory standards.
Beyond technical capability, the position requires strong analytical thinking and a methodical, investigative mindset. The Quality Product Analysis Specialist acts as a key liaison between warranty administration, customer service, and manufacturing partners—clearly communicating technical findings to ensure timely and fair claim resolution.
This role is essential in safeguarding product integrity, improving quality performance, and maintaining customer confidence through accurate, data-driven analysis and professional technical expertise.
Core Responsibilities
• Component Inspection: Conduct detailed physical and functional inspections on a wide range of components including turbos, braking systems, suspension units, clutches, and rotating electrics (alternators/starters).
• Diagnostic Testing: Operate specialised test equipment (e.g., vacuum testers, electronic actuator testers, battery/alternator analysers, brake DTV machines, and brake caliper testers) to verify part performance against factory specifications.
• Root Cause Analysis: Investigate and determine the underlying cause of failure (e.g., carbon buildup, oil starvation, electrical surges, installation errors) to support warranty claim evaluations.
• Warranty Claim Assessment: Review and assess warranty claims in accordance with company policies, determining validity and identifying potential manufacturing or usage defects.
• Digital Reporting & Documentation: Utilise computer systems to log findings, upload digital photos of defects, generate professional inspection and warranty evaluation reports, and maintain accurate records for claim processing.
• Quality & Compliance: Maintain a clean, organised laboratory/testing environment ensuring all test equipment is in safe and calibrated working order. Ensure inspections comply with company standards and relevant regulatory requirements.
• Cross-Functional Communication: Collaborate closely with warranty administration, customer service, and re manufacturing teams to share findings, explain technical details, and support timely claim resolution.
Technical Skills & Knowledge (Hard Skills)
• Multi-System Mastery: Deep mechanical knowledge of modern vehicle and electronic systems.
• Electrical Proficiency: Ability to read electrical schematics and use multimetres or oscilloscopes to test rotating electrics and electronic sensors.
• Software Literacy: Comfortable with PC-based diagnostic software, CRM portals, warranty management systems, and standard office tools (e.g., Microsoft Word/Excel).
• Precision Measurement: Skilled with precision tools such as micrometres, vernier calipers, and dial indicators for checking tolerances and shaft play.
• Warranty & Compliance Knowledge: Understanding of warranty policies, claim processing procedures, and applicable regulatory standards.
Character Qualities & Professionalism (Soft Skills)
• Analytical Thinking: Logical, detective-like mindset adept at solving complex diagnostic puzzles that other technicians may overlook.
• Attention to Detail: Precision in inspecting fracture surfaces, wear patterns, and minute electrical deviations.
• Reliability & Punctuality: Strict adherence to schedules and deadlines, ensuring customer and warranty reports are delivered on time.
• Clear Communication: Ability to translate complex technical failures into clear, simple language for non-technical stakeholders, customers, and internal teams.
• Collaboration: Effective team player with proven ability to coordinate across departments for efficient warranty handling.
Desired Qualifications & Experience
• Proven Experience: Ideally 3–5 years as a senior technician or diagnostic specialist in a high-volume garage, remanufacturing environment, or warranty inspection role.
• Certification: Level 3 Automotive Technician qualification or equivalent (e.g., IMI or City & Guilds).
• Failure Analysis Training. Warranty Training: Experience or formal training related to warranty claim evaluation and processing preferred.
Physical Requirements
• Capacity to safely handle heavy components (e.g., alternators, brake discs) and stand for extended periods in a workshop or laboratory environment.

Job Description:
Your impact
Are you ready to apply your studies to a real-world engineering challenge and gain practical experience of Systems Engineering?
At Leonardo, we're looking for summer placement students who are curious about how complex systems work, enjoy solving problems and want to gain experience working on projects that make a real-world difference. You'll have the opportunity to apply what you've learned at university, develop your technical and professional skills, and gain valuable insight into engineering in industry.
Our Summer Placement Programme
We have several exciting opportunities for Summer Placement Systems Engineering s within our Customer Support and Service Solutions (CS3) line of business. CS3 operates across the UK, developing and delivering innovative support solutions and services that help our customers keep critical capabilities available wherever and whenever they are needed.
Our nine-week Summer Placement is designed to give you meaningful experience within a relatively short period. You will typically work on a defined project or investigation focused on a real CS3 engineering challenge, giving you the opportunity to explore a problem, work with engineers and stakeholders, develop and evaluate ideas, and communicate your findings and recommendations. Projects are likely to support the development of CS3's engineering capability and could involve areas such as new technologies, data and information, engineering methods and tools, or new approaches to how we design and deliver support solutions. You will work as part of a team throughout your placement, whether undertaking a defined investigation or contributing to a broader range of ongoing engineering activities.
You won't be expected to know everything when you join. You'll also receive coaching and support from your team and our dedicated CS3 Early Careers Manager. You will also have opportunities to engage with other early careers colleagues and the wider engineering community, helping you gain an understanding of the different career opportunities available within Leonardo.
As your understanding and confidence grow, you'll have the opportunity to take ownership of elements of your project, explore ideas and apply what you've learned at university in a practical engineering environment. There will also be opportunities to get involved in STEM activities with local schools.

• Gather, analyse and interpret information or data to develop your understanding and support engineering decisions.
• Explore potential solutions, approaches or improvements, considering their benefits, limitations and wider implications.
• Use Systems Engineering techniques such as requirements analysis, modelling, option assessment or structured problem solving, where appropriate to your project.
• Work collaboratively with engineers and specialists from different disciplines, learning from their expertise and contributing your own ideas and perspectives.
• Develop practical experience of how engineering activities are undertaken within an organisation, including the processes, methods and tools used to deliver high-quality technical work.
• Document and communicate your work clearly, sharing your findings, conclusions or recommendations with relevant stakeholders.
• Contribute to engineering capability and process improvement, where relevant to your placement.
• Contribute to the design, development, integration, verification or support of complex systems and support solutions.
The exact activities will vary depending on the team and area you join, giving you the opportunity to develop a broad understanding of Systems Engineering while building your technical knowledge and practical experience.
What we need from you:
You will need:
• To be currently studying an undergraduate or postgraduate degree in a relevant discipline, such as Engineering, Physics, Mathematics, Computer Science or another STEM subject.
• An interest in engineering and enthusiasm for developing your understanding of Systems Engineering in an industry environment.
We are also looking for people who can demonstrate some of the following through their studies, university projects, work experience, extracurricular activities or other experiences:
• Curiosity and a logical approach to solving unfamiliar problems.
• Self-motivation and a proactive approach to learning and problem solving.
• The ability to consider both the detail of a problem and the wider system or context.
• A willingness to investigate a topic, ask questions and use evidence to develop your understanding.
• A collaborative approach and willingness to learn from, and share ideas with, people from different technical and professional backgrounds.
• The ability to organise and prioritise your work and take ownership of tasks, seeking guidance where appropriate.
• Confidence to ask questions, constructively challenge ideas and speak up when something doesn't look right.
• Clear written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to explain technical information and ideas to different audiences.
• A willingness to seek feedback, learn from experience and try new approaches.
You do not need previous experience of the defence or aerospace industry. We are interested in your potential, your approach to problem solving and your willingness to learn. This is not an exhaustive list, and we encourage you to apply even if you don't yet have experience in all of the areas above. We recognise that a Summer Placement is an opportunity to develop your skills and experience. Be part of one of the UK’s leading small animal referral centres!
Applications from highly motivated and ambitious colleagues are invited to undertake a Residency Training Programme in Veterinary Anaesthesia and Analgesia, commencing in February 2027.
Willows’ Anaesthesia team provides a comprehensive anaesthesia and analgesia service to referral patients from practices across the UK. Willows is a truly multi-disciplinary centre with Specialists across Soft Tissue Surgery, Neurology, Oncology, Ophthalmology, Cardiology, Dermatology, Orthopaedics, Internal Medicine, Diagnostic Imaging, Clinical Nutrition, Dentistry and ECC.
Facilities at Willows are second to none, including:

• Keep templates current with regulatory change, business requirements and lessons learned from negotiations

General
• Maintain accurate records of contract review status, risk logs and regulatory tracking within the team's systems
• Contribute to continuous improvement of TPRM legal processes, including standardisation and efficiency initiatives

• Understanding of regulatory frameworks relating to third-party risk, outsourcing and operational resilience, such as PRA/FCA Outsourcing Rules, Solvency II, DORA or similar frameworks, would be beneficial.

• Curious mindset with a desire to learn and develop expertise in an evolving regulatory landscape.
• Comfortable working autonomously within a collaborative team environment.

Audiences now move freely between screens, services and devices. Customers expect digital experiences that simply work. AI is changing how products are built, how content is made and how businesses run. For the organisations we serve, this is a moment to reinvent rather than tweak.
We help them work out what to build, and then we help them build it. Our work spans network and telecoms reinvention, customer experience, the way content is produced, managed and monetised, and the creation of new digital products and services.
As a Consultant, you will sit where consulting meets product delivery. You will help clients get clear on the problem and their ambition, and then stay involved as that thinking becomes a product, platform or service that real customers use. You don't need to be an engineer, but you will enjoy working alongside engineers, designers and data specialists. You will get into the detail and make the practical trade-offs that turn a good idea into something that ships.
Challenges you could work on
• Simplifying a telecoms operator's products and the systems behind them, so new services launch in weeks rather than years.
• Redesigning how consumers and businesses buy, set up and get help with their broadband, mobile and connectivity services.
• Modernising the platforms that bring programmes and live sport to audiences across apps, TVs and devices.
• Using AI to speed up how content is tagged, edited, localised and discovered.
• Creating new products, commercial models and revenue streams from content, audiences, advertising and intellectual property.
• Helping a betting or gaming operator improve how its products are designed, built and released.
• Changing the people, processes, technology and data behind a core part of a client's business, rather than simply replacing its systems.

• How Communications and Media businesses really work, from network to content to customer, by working with leading organisations in the sector.
• How to take an idea from discovery through to launch, drawing on Accenture's engineering, design, data and AI specialists.
• How to apply AI and data to real problems, and how to tell a promising use case from a distraction.

• Take responsibility for a defined product area or workstream, helping to move it from discovery and design through build, launch and improvement.

• You can point to outcomes you helped deliver for customers, operations or revenue.

• You have experience in, or a strong and growing understanding of, telecoms, media or both. Depth in one area, such as networks, broadcast, betting or publishing, matters more than breadth across all of them.

Working with clients and teams

bristolmyerssquibb.wd5.myworkdayjobs.com.description_excerpt:
At Bristol Myers Squibb, our employees often ask, “Who are you working for?”—a question that fuels collaboration, accountability, and urgency in our work. Our purpose-driven culture inspires us to discover, develop, and deliver innovative medicines to prevail over serious diseases. We offer uniquely interesting and meaningful work, opportunities for growth, and a supportive environment that values inclusion, wellbeing, flexibility, and comprehensive benefits. This is work that transforms the lives of patients, and the careers of those who do it.
Your work will reach patients. Let's talk about how.
Every medicine that makes it to a patient starts as a complex chemistry problem. Someone has to take a process that works seamlessly in a lab flask and make it work safely, reliably and at scale - in a manufacturing facility.
That someone could be you.
At Bristol Myers Squibb, we're looking for a Process Engineer to join our Chemical Process Development (CPD) team in Moreton, UK. CPD delivers clinical supplies and process development for all synthetic and anti-body drug conjugate (ADC) drug substances at BMS. This is a role where your engineering depth and your interpersonal skills will directly shape how - and how quickly - our clinical work reaches the patients who need them.
So, what does the role actually look like day-to-day?
You'll sit at the dynamic intersection between our internal science teams and the external Contract Development and Manufacturing Organisations (CDMOs) who bring our processes to life at scale.
On any given week, you might be:
• Reviewing a batch record for a hazardous chemistry campaign, making sure everything from safety and quality controls to process intent is technically accurate and operationally feasible  before it goes near a plant
• Walking a CDMO facility, either virtually or in person, assessing whether their equipment and capabilities are the right fit and if not, articulating exactly why and what needs to change
• Troubleshooting a manufacturing issue, drawing on your engineering fundamentals and collaboration skillset to find the root cause and get things back on track
• Presenting risk assessments and recommendations to leadership, translating complex technical realities into clear, actionable decisions
• Building strong relationships with CDMO partners across the world – to improve how we work together and so that when things get difficult (and sometimes they will), you already have the trust in the room
What's in it for you?
Let's be direct about the real value this role offers you as a professional:
• You'll work across the full range of chemical engineering unit operations — reaction, crystallisation, distillation, extraction, filtration, drying, and milling — applied to pharmaceutical small molecule/ADC scale-up.
• Real influence across teams and organisations This role demands - and rewards - the ability to drive technical negotiations, influence cross-functional teams, and build trusted working relationships with external partners. For the right person, this is where your interpersonal skills become as professionally valuable as your engineering ones.
• A global role with a local base You'll be based at our Moreton, UK site but working closely with colleagues across the Atlantic - including your direct line manager in the US – and with CDMOs around the world. With up to 50% remote working available, you get flexibility without losing the connection and collaboration that makes this kind of work rewarding.
• Variety beyond the desk Up to 20% international travel means you'll be on-site at CDMOs and in facilities.
• A platform to grow and give back BMS actively values mentorship and knowledge-sharing. Whether it's developing colleagues, contributing to communities of practice, or helping shape how the function works - this is a role where building others up is part of the job, not an afterthought.
Is this you?
• You'll bring a B.Eng. or M.Eng. in Chemical Engineering and at least 10–15 years of industrial manufacturing experience - ideally in pharmaceutical drug substance manufacturing and GMP environments. Experience in specialty chemical or petrochemical industries is also acceptable.
• You know how to read a lab protocol and visualise how it will operate in a manufacturing environment.
• You can spot scale-up risk before it becomes a manufacturing incident.
• You have a strong grounding in chemical engineering fundamentals across reaction, crystallisation, distillation, extraction, filtration, drying, and milling
• But just as importantly: you communicate clearly, you adapt your approach to the audience and the stakes, and you're comfortable managing complexity across multiple workstreams and stakeholders at once.
• Experience in lab-based small molecule development? Useful, but not essential.
Please note: This position requires work within facilities handling hazardous chemical agents, which, if improperly handled, may have the potential to affect employee health, including reproductive function and/or embryo/fetal development.
Why BMS, why now?
BMS is a company that has approved treatments that have genuinely changed what's possible in oncology, immunology, cardiovascular disease, and beyond. Our pipeline continues to grow — and the work of our Chemical Process Development team is central to keeping it moving.
When you get this right, patients get their medicine sooner. That's the job.
Ready to apply? We'd love to hear from you.

As a global leader in cybersecurity, CrowdStrike protects the people, processes and technologies that drive modern organizations. Since 2011, our mission hasn’t changed — we’re here to stop breaches, and we’ve redefined modern security with the world’s most advanced AI-native platform. We work on large scale distributed systems, processing almost 3 trillion events per day and this traffic is growing daily. Our customers span all industries, and they count on CrowdStrike to keep their businesses running, their communities safe and their lives moving forward. We're proud to work for a mission-driven company leveraging AI to transform the way we work. CrowdStrikers drive their careers through flexibility and autonomy while also being expected to contribute to a culture of responsible AI adoption, experimentation, and innovation. We use an AI-first mindset as a force multiplier to proactively and continuously accelerate execution, build expertise, uncover insights, and solve complex problems. We’re always looking to add talented CrowdStrikers to the team who have limitless passion, a relentless focus on innovation and a fanatical commitment to our customers, our community and each other. Ready to join a mission that matters? The future of cybersecurity starts with you.
About the Role
The Threat Analyst joins the Emerging Threats and Security Validation team within the CrowdStrike Malware Research Center (MRC). This team plays a critical role in understanding today's threat landscape, identifying gaps in Falcon's detection capabilities, and helping improve CrowdStrike's protection through threat research, automation, AI, and machine learning.
Working closely with Threat Research, Engineering, Data Science, and Red Team teams, you'll investigate emerging threats, validate detection coverage, and translate technical research into product improvements that better protect our customers. This is an excellent opportunity for someone who enjoys solving complex technical problems while making a direct impact on our products.
What You'll Do:
•
Research and analyse emerging malware and cyber threats to understand how they impact our customers.
•
Investigate malware across the full attack lifecycle (adversary kill chain) to ensure Falcon detects and stops threats at every stage.
•
Distinguish genuine threats from background noise by analysing data from multiple internal and external sources.
•
Validate and improve CrowdStrike's detection capabilities by identifying gaps and working with engineering teams to strengthen our protections.
•
Support external security testing and certification programmes (such as AV-Test, AV-Comparatives, and SE Labs) by analysing test results and helping address any missed detections.
•
Respond to newly discovered threats by performing technical investigations and recommending the best approach for detection and prevention.
•
Partner with Threat Research, Engineering, Red Team, and Machine Learning teams to translate research into product improvements.
•
Help design and improve automation that reduces manual effort and accelerates threat analysis.
•
Communicate technical findings clearly to engineering and response teams to enable faster and more effective action.
•
Contribute to the continuous evolution of Falcon by combining malware research, automation, AI, and machine learning to improve customer protection.
What You'll Need:
•
Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science or a related field.
•
4+ years of experience in threat research with a focus on malware analysis.
•
Experience reverse engineering file-based malware, exploits, and other attack techniques. Industry certifications such as GIAC Reverse Engineering Malware (GREM) are desirable.
•
Strong understanding of disassembly and structured programming principles.
•
Deep knowledge of at least one major operating system and its internals to support behaviour-based analysis.
•
Strong understanding of the adversary kill chain and attacker behaviour, with experience applying red team methodologies to validate defensive coverage. Certifications such as Offensive Security Certified Professional (OSCP) are desirable.
•
Experience collaborating with engineering teams to turn research into production capabilities.
•
Ability to develop small automation or scripting projects to solve immediate technical challenges.
•
Experience contributing to public security testing programmes (such as AV-Test, AV-Comparatives, or SE Labs) is a plus.
•
Experience working with large datasets and tools such as Splunk, Elasticsearch, or Kibana is a plus.
•
Proven experience utilizing AI technologies to enhance decision-making, streamline workflows and processes, improve efficiency and drive business outcomes.
About the Malware Research Center:
The CrowdStrike Malware Research Center is the core of Falcon’s malware detection and response capabilities. The team has a focus on understanding the threat landscape and sets the target for what Falcon should be identifying and preventing. Additionally, the MRC is responsible for understanding our capabilities, and mapping how well our machine learning and behavioral protection capabilities are doing against those threats. Where there is a gap, the MRC takes action to improve our detection stance, and improve our overall protection story. MRC also performs pathfinding research to enable technology development using innovation, prototyping and bleeding edge machine learning to support our flagship Falcon product. There are many parts of CrowdStrike working towards protecting customer environments, and the MRC works across all of them to ensure we are on target and providing the best protection for our current Threat landscape.
Emerging Threats and Security Validation Team:
Leading the charge for understanding the activity of malware today is the Emerging Threats and Security Validation team. With a focus on malware research, the primary role of the team is to understand the threats and malware that are affecting our customer’s businesses. The challenge is the enormous scale of malware today and the sheer number of samples required to be addressed, which requires a more creative approach than traditional Anti-Virus research. Using the data amassed from CrowdStrike’s capabilities and products, we take a holistic view of the threat landscape and identify the emerging threats that are likely to affect our business in the short to medium term. Human efforts are bolstered by automation, AI enrichment, and machine learning to protect our customers when they need it most.

Principal Responsibilities
Microsoft 365 Platform Ownership
• Own the product vision and experience for core Microsoft 365 services including Office apps, Teams, SharePoint and OneDrive, with Copilot as the primary accelerator.
• Define and maintain usage patterns, standards and guardrails for collaboration, content storage and productivity.
• Partner with service owning teams to influence roadmap decisions, prioritisation and technical outcomes.
• Balance innovation with operational stability, compliance and user simplicity.
Collaboration and Stakeholder Engagement
• Act as the primary point of contact for Copilot and assigned M365 apps.
• Engage with stakeholders across business units (e.g., Investment, Back Office, Sales, IT, Compliance).

Product Ownership & Strategy
• Develop and maintain a unified product roadmap across Copilot and core M365 services, ensuring capabilities land in a way that improves how people actually work day to day.

• Prioritize features and enhancements based on business value and user feedback.
• Own the product backlog, ensuring clarity and alignment with organizational priorities.
Implementation & Adoption
• Drive adoption of standard collaboration models across Teams, SharePoint and OneDrive.
• Ensure Office applications are configured and evolved to support modern, AI assisted ways of working.
• Reduce complexity and duplication across M365 by simplifying choices for end users.
User Experience & Value Realization
• Champion end user experience across Microsoft 365, using Copilot to amplify productivity while ensuring the underlying M365 experience is intuitive, consistent and trusted.
• Gather and analyse user feedback, usage data, and adoption metrics.
• Identify and address barriers to adoption and maximize business value.
Governance & Compliance

Technical Expertise:

Overview
Houlihan Lokey, Inc. (NYSE:HLI) is a leading global investment bank recognized for delivering independent strategic and financial advice to corporations, financial sponsors, and governments. With uniquely deep industry expertise, broad international reach, and a partnership approach rooted in trust, the firm provides innovative, integrated solutions across mergers and acquisitions, capital solutions, financial restructuring, and financial and valuation advisory. Our unmatched transaction volumes provide differentiated, data-driven perspectives that help our clients achieve their most critical goals. To learn more about Houlihan Lokey, please visit HL.com.
Corporate Finance
The Houlihan Lokey Corporate Finance business has extensive expertise in mergers, acquisitions, divestitures, activist shareholder and takeover defense, and other related advisory services for a broad range of clients. In addition, we have the proven ability to engineer and execute financing solutions that are essential for growth and success and offer access to financing in the public and alternative capital markets through the issuance of debt, equity, or hybrid securities. In EMEA, we work with a wide spectrum of companies, from middle-market privately owned enterprises to large multinational organizations. With a growing platform of Corporate Finance professionals and offices across the region, in addition to our global reach and in-depth knowledge across a broad range of industries, we have the breadth and targeted expertise to provide exceptional client service.
Industrials
Houlihan Lokey’s Industrials Group has earned a reputation for providing superior service and achieving outstanding results in M&A advisory, capital raising, restructuring, and valuation.
Our transaction quality and client work benefit from our company culture, where the senior team are highly engaged in the execution of client projects, and from our experience as leaders in the market for over a decade, which has given our professionals valuable exposure to a variety of situations and challenges. In 2025, our Industrials Group was ranked as the No. 1 M&A advisor for global Industrials transactions. With a team of over 50 bankers across Europe and 170 globally, it is an exciting time to join our growing Industrials team.
Scope
The Industrials team at Houlihan Lokey are looking to add a Senior Analyst or Associate in London or Manchester.
The environment at Houlihan Lokey is both collegial and entrepreneurial. Teamwork is essential to the firm’s success. At the same time, creativity and new ideas are encouraged. Senior Analysts / Associates are given substantial responsibility and are encouraged to help us grow our business.
Senior Analysts and Associates work on transactions that provide exposure to various investment banking services, including M&A, private placements of debt and equity, refinancings, and leveraged buyouts.
Responsibilities
As a Senior Analyst / Associate, you will:
• Prepare, analyse and help explain historical and projected financial information.
• Create financial models.
• Coordinate and perform business due diligence.
• Prepare confidential information memoranda, management presentations, marketing pitches and other presentations.
• Value companies and businesses.
• Lead the planning and execution of marketing engagements.
• Build relationships and maintain direct contact with clients and prospective clients, professional advisors and other stakeholders.
• Supervise junior staff members in financial analyses.
• Assist in the marketing and planning of engagements.
Requirements / Qualifications
The environment at Houlihan Lokey is results-driven and entrepreneurial and, as such, rewards top performers with substantial responsibility and interaction with senior-level professionals and clients.
The Following Qualifications Are Required
• You will have a strong academic track record and achieved a 2:1 or equivalent degree
• 2-4 years of investment banking experience within M&A Advisory. Experience in the Industrials sector favourable
• Fundamental understanding of financial valuation methodologies, and applications
• Advanced Financial modeling and analytical abilities; Strong LBO and DCF modelling skills
• Strong qualitative and quantitative research skills
• Understanding of financial statements analysis with the ability to work through key assumptions, implicit caveats, and limitations
• Excellent verbal and written communication skills in English are essential
• Strong knowledge of Excel
• Independent thinker and resourceful problem solver driven to succeed
• Strong work ethic, organizational skills and ability to multitask is crucial
• Motivated and demonstrated ability to work cooperatively with all levels of staff in a rapidly changing, demanding, but ultimately rewarding environment
• Ability to work independently in a fast-paced environment

Title:
FP&A Principal Analyst
KBR is a global provider of differentiated, professional services and technologies delivered across a wide government, defense and industrial base. We are looking for a commercially focused finance professional to support the Europe & North Africa Finance Director within the STS business.
This role will play a key part in consolidating regional financial performance, supporting month-end close activities, driving working capital improvements, and helping operational leaders understand business performance across the region.

Regional Financial Consolidation & Reporting
• Consolidate monthly financial performance across the Europe & North Africa region.

• Assist in coordinating submissions across multiple business units and countries.
• Ensure financial reporting is accurate, timely, and aligned across the region.
Month-End & Forecast Support
• Support the month-end close process, including revenue, margin, and cost analysis.
• Assist with quarterly forecasts, annual budgets, and longer-term planning cycles.
• Work closely with operational finance teams to understand movements in project performance and forecast changes.
• Help improve forecast accuracy and consistency across the region.
Working Capital & Cash Focus
• Support initiatives to improve cash performance across the business.
• Work with project and operational teams to reduce aged Accounts Receivable (AR) balances and resolve unbilled positions.
• Track overdue debtors and support escalation/follow-up activities where required.
• Assist in identifying process improvements to strengthen billing and cash collection performance.
Business Partnering
• Build strong relationships with operational leaders and project teams across the region.
• Support finance directors and business leaders with ad hoc analysis and commercial insight.
• Help translate financial data into clear business-focused messaging and actions.
• Support operational reviews and regional performance discussions.
Process & Reporting Improvement
• Support continuous improvement of reporting processes and management information.
• Work with wider FP&A and reporting teams to improve consistency and efficiency.
• Assist with development and enhancement of Power BI reporting and dashboard capabilities.
• Support alignment of reporting processes as the business evolves under the new regional structure.
Skills & Experience
• A relevant number of years of experience in finance, FP&A, project finance, or operational finance.
• Qualified Accountant (ACA, ACCA, CIMA, CPA or equivalent)
• Strong Excel and financial modelling capability.
• Experience supporting month-end close, forecasting, and financial analysis.
• Comfortable working with large data sets and multiple stakeholders.  Strong attention to detail with the ability to simplify and communicate key messages clearly.
• Experience with Power BI, EPM, FCCS, SAP, or Microsoft Dynamics would be beneficial.
• Experience in project-based, engineering, consulting, or services businesses preferred.
Personal Attributes
• Proactive and commercially minded.
• Comfortable operating in a fast-paced environment with changing priorities.
• Strong communicator with the confidence to engage with operational stakeholders.
• Willing to challenge where needed while maintaining strong working relationships.
• Team-oriented with a hands-on approach.
KBR Company Information
When you become part of the KBR team, your opportunities are endless. Through collaboration with our customers, we’re defining tomorrow’s challenges, then providing the solutions and services to overcome those challenges, always maintaining our commitment to total safety and reliability.
At KBR, we partner with government and industry clients to provide purposeful and comprehensive solutions with an emphasis on efficiency and safety. With a full portfolio of services, proprietary technologies and expertise, our employees are ready to handle projects and missions throughout their entire lifecycle, from planning and design to sustainability and maintenance. Whether at the bottom of the ocean or in outer space, our clients trust us to deliver the impossible on a daily basis.
Working at KBR means being rewarded for your contributions. In addition to competitive benefits and professional development, our people are empowered to use all their potential, creating meaningful change for themselves and our clients. We attract the best minds in the world because our expertise thrives on creativity, resourcefulness and collaboration. That is how we supply our clients with cutting-edge solutions and services.
As the needs of the world change, we’re ready to respond and guide the way forward with strategic, sustainable, and technological advancements grounded in more than a century of practical application and execution.

Responsibilities:
As the Category Manager, you will support and manage indirect and services spend across the business, partnering with function leads in areas such as Facilities, Logistics, Recruitment, Marketing & IT, but not limited to these categories.
You will act as the procurement lead and commercial partner for assigned indirect categories, balancing service quality, operational needs, cost, compliance, contractual protection and supplier performance.
For this you will understand and drive the:
Category Profile
• Develop and implement category strategies for assigned service categories in collaboration with functional stakeholders.
• Ensure category strategies align with Apollo business objectives and support growth, profitability, operational excellence and sustainability goals.
• Understand historical spend trends and business drivers to forecast future requirements, sourcing activity and budget impact.
• Build and maintain category roadmaps covering savings, contract renewals, supplier development, risk management and sustainability initiatives.
• Establish sourcing strategies based on total cost of ownership, service outcomes and contractual risk rather than purchase price alone.
Stakeholder Partnerships
• Build strong working relationships with Facilities, Logistics, Recruitment, Marketing, IT, HR, Finance and other business leaders.
• Act as the primary procurement lead for assigned functions and become a trusted business partner.
• Challenge requirements constructively while ensuring stakeholder objectives are understood and achieved.
• Facilitate cross-functional decision-making on sourcing, supplier selection, service scopes, SLAs and contract positions.
• Support business stakeholders through supplier escalations, contract queries and service performance issues.
• Promote procurement best practice, contract discipline and governance throughout the organisation.
Contract Strategy, Governance & Commercial Protection
• Own the contract lifecycle for assigned spend categories, from tender and negotiation through implementation, renewal, extension and termination.
• Develop contracting strategies that balance commercial value, operational flexibility, service accountability, supplier performance and business risk.
• Lead negotiation of all required agreements, for the different functions and requirements
• Act as the procurement subject matter expert for commercial contract terms and conditions
• Evaluate and negotiate contract terms covering performance, risk allocation, compliance, business continuity and governance requirements.
• Ensure all contracts contain clear scope, deliverables, pricing schedules, payment terms, SLA and KPI requirements, reporting obligations and governance arrangements.
• Challenge supplier-proposed contractual positions and negotiate commercially balanced agreements that protect Apollo's interests.
• Maintain visibility of contract expiry dates, renewal notice periods, extension options, price review mechanisms, indexation clauses and benchmarking opportunities.
• Proactively identify opportunities to renegotiate contracts to improve commercial value, reduce risk, resolve service issues and deliver efficiency improvements.
• Ensure contractual commitments are fully understood by business stakeholders and are effectively managed throughout the life of the agreement.
• Develop and maintain contract templates, commercial standards, negotiation playbooks and contract review checklists to improve procurement effectiveness.
• Review and interpret contractual pricing schedules, indexation mechanisms, minimum volume commitments and termination costs.
• Deliver cost reduction programmes and value-added initiatives across assigned categories.
• Utilise TCO and TCA methodologies to evaluate and compare sourcing options.
• Support annual budget planning through cost forecasting, contract review and market intelligence.
Supplier Relationship Management
• Build strategic relationships with key service providers and develop supplier segmentation and relationship management plans.
• Conduct regular business reviews with strategic suppliers and hold suppliers accountable to agreed contractual obligations.
• Establish scorecards measuring cost, service, quality, responsiveness, innovation, contractual compliance and sustainability.
• Identify opportunities for suppliers to deliver continuous improvement and innovation.
• Manage supplier development programmes where service performance or contract compliance requires improvement.
Risk Management & Compliance
• Maintain supplier and category risk assessments, including contractual, commercial, financial, operational, service continuity, compliance and reputational risks.
• Evaluate supplier financial health, service capability, scalability, resilience, insurance levels and business continuity arrangements.
• Develop risk mitigation plans and contingency strategies for critical services.
• Monitor market developments that could impact service continuity, capacity or cost.
• Support supplier audits and compliance assessments as required.
• Ensure suppliers comply with Apollo policies, ethical sourcing requirements, data protection obligations and sustainability expectations.
Sustainability & ESG
• Integrate sustainability objectives into category strategies, tender assessments, supplier selection and contract requirements.
• Support Apollo's Net Zero and wider sustainability commitments.
• Encourage suppliers to improve environmental, social and governance performance and provide appropriate sustainability reporting.
• Drive initiatives that reduce environmental impacts and improve responsible procurement practices across services spend.
Data & Reporting
• Develop and maintain category dashboards and performance metrics.
• Produce insights into expenditure, supplier performance, contract coverage, savings delivery, renewal pipeline and risk exposure.
• Present recommendations and business cases to stakeholders and leadership teams.
• Maintain accurate procurement records, supplier information and contract data within company systems.
Continuous Improvement
• Identify opportunities to improve procurement processes, systems, templates and controls.
• Drive standardisation and procurement governance across all spend categories.
• Support digital procurement initiatives and automation opportunities.
• Promote a culture of continuous improvement, compliance and value creation.

At Waythrough, we’re looking for a compassionate and motivated Social Isolation Support Coordinator to join our Community Services team. • Experience working with vulnerable adults, older people or individuals with wellbeing needs.
• An understanding of the causes and impact of loneliness and social isolation.
• Experience assessing individual needs and developing support plans.
• Knowledge of safeguarding principles and procedures.

• The ability to motivate and empower individuals to achieve positive outcomes.

Who are we
Founded in 1896, Knight Frank was registered as Knight Frank LLP a Limited Liability Partnership, on 3 November 2003, registered in England & Wales at 55 Baker Street, London, W1U 8AN with the registered number of OC305934. Headquartered in London, UK, Knight Frank is one of the world's leading independent real estate consultancies. We work responsibly in partnership to enhance people's lives and environments in over 50 Markets, 600+ Offices, 20,000+ People, 1 Global Network.
At the heart of all we do are our Clients. A relationship built on trust is vital. As trusted partners in property, we act with integrity and care, understanding our clients’ unique needs and consistently thinking about the bigger picture to provide personalised, clear and considered advice across all areas of property. Through our deep understanding of key markets and sectors – both emerging and established – we are dedicated to meeting and exceeding their property goals.
A true partnership is a balanced one, and our People are passionate about, and committed to, making our business inclusive and diverse. We give every individual the space and opportunity to perform at their best and be recognised for the immense value they bring. We empower everyone to have autonomy in their role and encourage them to use their voice in how we can make a positive impact as a firm and shape the future of real estate, the built environment and the impact on the communities we serve. Our collaborative and engaged teams provide excellent and dedicated client service. In our workplace, opinions are respected, everyone is invited to contribute to the success of our business and innovation, and new ideas are celebrated.
In 2021 we celebrated our 125th anniversary and set out Our Desired Future, cemented in three pillars: People Potential, Client Centricity and always Creating our Future, together. Learn more about what sets us apart here.
About The Role
Knight Frank is launching a new Affiliate Broker model, created for experienced residential brokers who want to build their own business with the backing of one of the world’s most respected property brands.
This opportunity is focused on key markets where Knight Frank does not currently operate through its Bristol City network. You’ll represent your own defined territory, operating independently while being fully aligned to Knight Frank’s global platform.
As a self‑employed Affiliate Broker, you’ll manage sales end to end, grow your own pipeline and build a personal brand, all with the credibility, reach and infrastructure of Knight Frank behind you.
Why this opportunity stands out:
• Run your own business within the Knight Frank brand representing you
• Operate in a market not currently covered by our Bristol Residential office
• 50% commission on all completed deals, plus referral income across our global network
• Marketing support.
• Access to CRM, portals, marketing collateral, photography and floorplans
• Worldwide referrals across 150+ service lines and 20,000 property professionals
• Centralised compliance, admin and operational support so you can focus on clients
You control your diary, your clients and your growth, with no ceiling on earnings.
Who this suits:
• Established residential sales professionals
• Brokers with strong local knowledge/contacts, or the ambition to own a defined market, supported by the largest privately owned property company across the globe
• Entrepreneurial, self‑motivated individuals ready to step beyond the traditional office model
What makes it different:
This is a business opportunity, not a job. You get the freedom of self‑employment, combined with the strength, credibility, and global reach of Knight Frank.
If you are ready to start something of your own with the backing of Knight Frank, in a market or neighbourhood you know you can build an exceptional business in, we’d like to hear from you.
Register your interest today.
Competitive salary

Knight Frank is seeking a talented Data Centres Surveyor or Senior Surveyor to join our growing Data Centre Valuation & Advisory team in London. This is an exciting opportunity to become part of a market-leading team that has experienced significant growth and is recognised as the largest dedicated data centre consultancy and valuation team across EMEA.

• Leased facilities
• Development sites
• Portfolio and fund valuations
• Transaction underwriting
• Vendor and commercial due diligence

• Analyse complex financial and operational information to support valuation assignments.
• Build, maintain, and refine discounted cash flow (DCF) models.
• Review client financial statements, construction contracts, power agreements, and legal due diligence documentation.
• Conduct financial and commercial analysis to inform valuation assumptions.
• Support project leaders on high-profile valuation and advisory mandates.
• Contribute to market research and analysis of data centre sector dynamics.
• Assist in preparing valuation reports and client deliverables.

• Experience creating or amending DCF models.
• Background in property valuation, finance, real estate, investment analysis, or a related field.
• Advanced Microsoft Excel skills.
• Excellent attention to detail and organisational skills.
• A proactive attitude and willingness to learn.
• Strong communication and problem-solving abilities.
Desirable:
• Knowledge of Argus Enterprise.
• MRICS qualification or progress towards professional accreditation.
